name: Prompt Block with Exit Status
note: Warp-style command blocks: each finished command carries a coloured exit-code chip, a left accent rail and a duration on the right. The live block shows path + git branch and types the next command behind a blinking block cursor. Reduced motion pins the command and stops the cursor.

name: Command Palette
note: Fuzzy command palette with a ⌘K badge, a blinking query caret, highlighted match characters and right-aligned key bindings. The selection walks the list on its own so the widget reads as live; reduced motion leaves the first row selected.

name: Git Status Panel
note: git status -sb rendered properly: branch with ahead/behind counters, the two-column XY porcelain code (staged green, unstaged red, ?? untracked) and per-file diffstat. The loop stages one file at a time with a green flash, updates the counter, then resets to unstaged.

name: Diff Viewer with Gutters
note: Unified diff with dual line-number gutters, a +/- sign column and tinted add/delete rows, under a real hunk header. Lines cascade in on a loop like a diff painting itself; reduced motion shows the whole hunk at rest.

name: Package Install Progress
note: A pnpm add run: braille spinner, live percentage, gradient progress bar, fluctuating throughput and resolved/reused counters, with installed packages sliding into the log as they land. Completes to a green check and 'done in 3.4s', then restarts. Reduced motion renders the finished state.

name: Test Run Summary
note: A vitest run resolving file by file: each row spins, then settles to a green check or red cross while the passed/failed tallies and the elapsed clock tick up. The failing assertion slides in at the end, then the run replays. Space for the error line is reserved so nothing jumps.

note: zsh-autosuggestions behaviour: as the prefix is typed a dim ghost completion trails the cursor, the history list filters live with the matched prefix highlighted, and the best match is selected. Pressing accept turns the whole line green, then it clears and types the next stem.
